QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_37

question.text: Per Ch 4.3.2, it is crucial to assess both positive and negative UNINTENDED impacts of the project at the pre-listing stage in order to:

answer.text: Either screen out potential issues or implement measures to design the project intervention so that unintended negative impacts are mitigated or minimised

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 4.3.2, pre-listing assessment of unintended impacts (both positive and negative) supports two possible actions: screen out problematic projects, or redesign intervention to mitigate unintended negative impacts. This is central to responsible project design. The Trap: A, C, D suggest avoidance/manipulation — the opposite of the chapter's ethical stance. Cross-Exam Context: Unintended-impact assessment is tested in SAS-500, SAS-1100, SAS-1300 (XXIII Ch 7) and parallels ESG negative-screening in investment practice (XIX-A/B/C/D/E AIF). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Always ask: 'What harms could this project cause?' (e.g., livelihood displacement, cultural disruption, dependency creation). Bury unintended negative impacts in a footnote only after designing mitigation — never omit them.
